headline_marked: Paltan: [[CPB office attacked]] over alleged Awami League ties
headline: Paltan: CPB office attacked over alleged Awami League ties
summary: Activists from the CPB's youth and student wings claim BNP-affiliated groups stormed the headquarters in Dhaka's Purana Paltan after a celebratory rally.
details: The Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB) headquarters in Dhaka’s Purana Paltan came under attack on Monday night, allegedly over the party's ties with the banned Awami League.

Activists from the CPB's affiliated Jubo Union and Bangladesh Students’ Union claim that members of the BNP, Jubo Dal, and Chhatra Dal carried out the assault after the chanting of the 'Joy Bangla' slogan.
The incident occurred after 9pm following the release of former Students’ Union president Dipak Shil from custody, as members held a celebratory rally in Paltan.
The confrontation escalated as a crowd converged outside and stormed the premises of Mukti Bhaban, where the CPB offices are located on the fifth and sixth floors.
Students’ Union President Mahir Shahriar reported that attackers attempted to brand the party as Awami League and that leaders were trapped inside the building.
CPB General Secretary Abdullah Al Kafi stated he was heading to the premises after learning that a mob had assaulted the party headquarters.
However, Paltan Police chief Ariful Alam denied any assault or injuries, stating that while tension flared during the celebratory march, police were deployed to manage the scene.
Earlier on Monday, police had detained Dipak Shil from Dhanmondi Road 27 during a demonstration protesting the barring of female Baul folk singers from performing in Sunamganj.
caption:
A mob stormed the CPB headquarters in Dhaka's Purana Paltan after a celebratory rally turned violent.

The Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB) headquarters in Dhaka’s Purana Paltan came under attack on Monday night, allegedly over the party's ties with the banned Awami League.

Activists from the CPB's affiliated Jubo Union and Bangladesh Students’ Union claim that members of the BNP, Jubo Dal, and Chhatra Dal carried out the assault after the chanting of the 'Joy Bangla' slogan.

The incident occurred after 9pm following the release of former Students’ Union president Dipak Shil from custody, as members held a celebratory rally in Paltan.

The confrontation escalated as a crowd converged outside and stormed the premises of Mukti Bhaban, where the CPB offices are located on the fifth and sixth floors.

Students’ Union President Mahir Shahriar reported that attackers attempted to brand the party as Awami League and that leaders were trapped inside the building.

CPB General Secretary Abdullah Al Kafi stated he was heading to the premises after learning that a mob had assaulted the party headquarters.

However, Paltan Police chief Ariful Alam denied any assault or injuries, stating that while tension flared during the celebratory march, police were deployed to manage the scene.

Earlier on Monday, police had detained Dipak Shil from Dhanmondi Road 27 during a demonstration protesting the barring of female Baul folk singers from performing in Sunamganj.
